hypothesis_title: Thalamocortical Coupling Modulates Insomnia Severity via Structural Morphology and White Matter Integrity
scientific_question: Test whether Thalamocortical Coupling Modulates Insomnia Severity via Structural Morphology and White Matter Integrity is supported by available analysis-ready variables.
hypothesis_summary: This hypothesis proposes that thalamocortical coupling modulates insomnia severity through a dual pathway involving structural morphology and white matter integrity, integrating multimodal neuroimaging data.
hypothesis_content: Thalamocortical coupling modulates insomnia severity through a dual pathway involving structural morphology of the thalamus and white matter integrity, as measured by MRI and DTI, respectively. This pathway integrates both functional and structural neuroimaging data to explain the neurobiological basis of insomnia severity.

primary_tests.question: Does thalamocortical coupling (thalamus_DMN_FC) modulate insomnia severity (PSQI)?
Does structural morphology (thalamus_volume) modulate insomnia severity (PSQI)?
Does white matter integrity (FA) modulate insomnia severity (PSQI)?

analysis_plan: Conduct a multimodal neuroimaging study combining EEG-fMRI, MRI, and DTI in a cohort of insomnia patients. Measure thalamocortical coupling (thalamus_DMN_FC), structural morphology (thalamus_volume), and white matter integrity (FA). Use regression models to assess the relationship between thalamocortical coupling and insomnia severity, mediated by structural morphology and white matter integrity.

risks: Limited sample size (n=5 for most variables) may reduce statistical power.
Missing data in some EEG features (e.g., slow_wave_density, beta_power) may affect covariate control.
Potential confounding from scale variables (e.g., anxiety_score, depression_score) not fully accounted for in regression models.
llm_experiment_design.rationale: The analysis plan leverages available variables (thalamus_DMN_FC, thalamus_volume, FA) directly linked to the hypothesis. Structural morphology (thalamus_volume) and white matter integrity (FA) are selected as mediators based on their presence in the data. Risks include small sample size, missing EEG data, and potential confounding from scale variables.
